stemMd: Which statement about first ionization energy is correct?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It is always zero for metals.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It is the energy required to remove a proton from the nucleus.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It measures the number of neutrons in an atom.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It is the energy released when a liquid freezes.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It is the minimum energy required to remove an electron from an isolated neutral gaseous atom in its ground state.

explanationMd: First ionization concerns removal of an electron from a neutral gaseous atom to make a singly positive gaseous ion. Energy is needed to overcome attraction to the nucleus. The gaseous reference state separates this atomic property from lattice and phase-change effects.

distractorRationale.d: That is related to a phase change, not electron removal.
distractorRationale.c: Neutron count is not an energy of ionization.
distractorRationale.a: Removing electrons from gaseous metal atoms still requires energy.
distractorRationale.b: Proton removal is a nuclear process, not ionization.
